tagline: Down the north bank of the James, plantation lane by lane.
intro: Out of Richmond, Route 5 heads east along the north bank of the James on the line of older colonial roads, through Henrico, Charles City and James City, three of the eight shires of 1634. One after another the old James River plantations come along the road, from Shirley at the west end to Sherwood Forest.

Beside the highway runs the Virginia Capital Trail, a paved path for bicycles and walkers kept apart from the cars by a strip of vegetation and carried over streams and marsh on about 30 wooden bridges. Between Charles City and James City counties the road crosses the Chickahominy on a fixed bridge that replaced Barrett's Ferry.

moments.title: Berkeley Plantation
moments.text: At Harrison's Landing, the plantation's old wharf, the bugle call "Taps" was written in 1862 and first played here.

moments.title: Charles City
moments.text: A county seat of about a hundred people, gathered round a courthouse that has stood since the 1750s, about two miles up from the James.

moments.title: Sherwood Forest Plantation
moments.text: John Tyler retired here from the White House and renamed the place Sherwood Forest, to say the Whig party had made him an outlaw.
